# JClaw User Guide

> JClaw is a workbench for building, running, and watching AI agents. These files are its user guide, one Markdown file per section, in the order the app shows them.

The JClaw app shows the same text on its User Guide page. The pages are written for that page, so their links point into the app. A link such as `/guide#tasks-cron-syntax` names a section of the guide: the part after `#` starts with a file name below (`tasks`), and the rest is that file's heading (`## Cron syntax`), or the `{#id}` written after it. Other links that start with `/`, such as `/chat` or `/settings`, are screens in the JClaw app.

## User guide

- [Getting Started](getting-started.md): what JClaw is, your first five minutes, the sidebar, and the Guided Tour
- [Chat](chat.md): picking an agent, sending messages, attachments, voice mode, slash commands, tool calls, exports, and coding runs
- [Prompts](prompts.md): the Prompts Library of saved prompts, shared by all agents
- [Agents](agents.md): the main agent and custom agents, and setting an agent's model, system prompt, tools, skills, and MCP servers
- [Conversations & Channels](conversations-and-channels.md): searching and exporting conversations, and connecting agents to Slack, Telegram, and WhatsApp
- [Subagents](subagents.md): child agents an agent starts during a turn, their spawn and context modes, external coding harnesses, and sandboxing
- [Scrapes](scrapes.md): reading a website to a chosen depth, inside a chat turn or as a background scrape
- [Tasks](tasks.md): agent work that runs later or on a schedule, cron syntax, timezones, retention, and task runs
- [Reminders](reminders.md): scheduled messages delivered word for word, with no model call
- [Subagents, Tasks, or Reminders?](subagents-tasks-reminders.md): how the three compare, and which one to choose
- [Skills, Tools & MCP Servers](skills-tools-mcp.md): the three ways to give an agent new capabilities
- [Apps](apps.md): small static web apps JClaw hosts, and their `app.json` manifest
- [Settings](settings.md): every section of the Settings page, from providers to security; the longest file
- [Memories](memory.md): how agents capture facts after each turn, recall them later, and how to tune that
- [Logs & Dashboard](logs-and-dashboard.md): the Dashboard home page, the Logs page, and the sidebar status pip
